column1: response

I’m concerned that if people can use AI at home, they may wonder why they need to see a doctor if doctors use the same AI. This could make people rely too much on AI instead of getting proper medical care.
The concern is the accuracy/integrity of the training data used by the AI to provide assistance

AI can always make mistakes, but so can healthcare professionals. But it might be helpful for them to make less mistakes, for example a healthcare professional who deals with a lot of patients can sometimes mix up his thoughts, which rarely happens but it can happen. They can then give a wrong dose or a medicament that is conflicting with another one and can harm the patient. For me relying on AI for complete assessment is totally wrong. But thinking out loud with one can help straightening up the professional's thoughts and possibly lead to a more correct decision in cases of confusion.
I think the use of AI in healthcare works as a catalyst and expedites the entire process of diagnosis for patients, and summarizing reports.
I'm comfortable with healthcare and AI as long as the doctor uses his knowledge to agree or disagree on the diagnosis, blindly using AI would make serious issues
Accuracy

Use of AI is very useful but in an appropriate manner, It can also sometimes diagnose critical situations byt the final decision should always be based on doctor's or physician's experience and knowledge.
Knowing that the AI used has reputable database of the concerned healthcare issues will make it trustworthy to me.

Ai tools can miss symptoms or vital signs as well as hallucinate medical information. My concern is not about the person who use the tool but the tool itself and how reliable it is. Oftentimes it’s hard to detect AI mistakes and in a sensitive field like medical where it could be a life or death situation and multiplication the risk becomes higher.

When the professionals have questions, if they use AI rather than discussing with other professionals, it will cause me to be concerned whether the professionals does have the ability to fulfill his/her profession in this field.
I think that it would not be very professional for a healthcare provider to rely solely on AI for a diagnosis. But it would also depend on how AI is used in the healthcare tool.
If you care about the world and future generations, you won’t use AI

I am concerned about the accuracy of AI-based healthcare tools and their ability to understand complex medical conditions. However, I am reassured by the potential for AI to enhance diagnostic capabilities and improve patient outcomes.

Oh and by the way, if you're still looking for respondents, surveyswap.io really helped me when I was running a survey myself last year. You fill in surveys from others and get free respondents in return. Perhaps it's also helpful to you. Anyway, good luck with the study!
It shouldn't be used as a deciding factor for anything that is supposed to be the judgment of a professional medical expert
There are non-chatbot based AI tools that can be used, and will probably be more useful and less problematic than the chatbot based AI.

I am concerned about ai doing a classic "doctor Google", where a person enters their symptoms, the ai highlights the most probable diagnoses and also the most disastrous one, the person is then left distraught and worried for no good reason. ...healthcare professionals need to always remain present to correctly interpret symptoms and interpret ai output. ... I think ai can be used for the most simple, routine, not at all dangerous diseases or things that rely on pure pattern recognition like analyzing blood tests etc, this could take workload off the professionals so they can focus on more important work. It reassures me that the professional always remains responsible for caring for me

My pharmacist uses AI for their phone-call assistant which is fine, but anything healthcare related I think is unacceptable. You can't know what data the AI has been trained on; professionals have spent years training so there is no need to use AI for diagnoses. I think for admin work is fine though if needed.

TO MANY BUGS, A COMMON GENERATIVE RESPONSE

Accuracy. My medical records are full of errors. That's gotten worse wirh AI scribing. Now I get discharge documents and if I point out concerns (e.g. advising me to use loop diuretics to treat K+ about 2.5 as measured on BMP) doctors say "Oh, this isn't about you, it's AI." Then let me negotiate my cardiac meds with a symptom checker so at least SOMEONE human is involved. The hospital has notified me twice that I have cancer, because AI sees me referred to a doctor in another specialty who deals with a lot of cancer patients. My doctor has no reason to suspect that I have cancer. But I am prompted to sign up for chemo.

I use ChatGPT to help me interpret blood results and check what my nephrologist says. The interpretations are pretty accurate and align with what my nephrologist says. I wish my first nephrologist would have used AI, he didn't catch anything. My new nephrologist probably does not use AI.
it concerns me because it lessened the effort and responsibility of actions taken by the person, they can just blame ai, even if it makes them look bad
As long as the AI is checked by a person, preferably two, I'm fine with it helping make things more efficient.

I just hope that it's used only to narrow down the diagnosis variations, and not to make the full healthcare plan. I would prefer if my medical professional made their own decisions, and if they needed some assistance, then I'm willing to look over it.

All major AIs have been verifiably proven to blatantly LIE including verifiable LIES and refusal to provide information about health pharma product safety topics. But then the same can be said for human "doctors"

In my opinion, the use of AI in healthcare should be limited because if a doctors count only on AI to work they would eventually be dependent on it, it would be hard for people to find a doctor that knows his job in situations where there is no AI or internet access (in a plane for example).

The only concern I have is providing medical advice, as currently AI's advice about general queries is always supportive/ yes mannish, which worries me because, if that same kind of advice were to come out in response to medical issues, I have problems trusting it.

I have family members in the medical field working with AI for operations and symptom recordings, and I believe that as long as a medical expert is able to assess and fully evaluate (confirm) the outcome of AI, I have basic trust for their diagnosis. However, the trust very much depends on ethics of that medical expert, and I do not have confidence to trust every medical worker.
I am concerned that doctors may rely entirely on AI instead of using their own professional judgment. AI should support medical decisions, not replace the doctor’s responsibility.
